subject.title: [Bug]: browser upload/file chooser flow is flaky and can misreport stale-click failures as browser control timeouts

question: Should Browser upload continue to support paths-only arm-then-later-click as a first-class workflow, or should agent/tool flows be moved toward atomic upload-with-trigger or direct input targeting for dynamic pages?
rationale: Both paths-only arming and upload-with-trigger/direct-input forms are currently supported and documented-adjacent, so the remaining fix affects Browser API compatibility and agent guidance rather than only a local defect.

options.title: Compatibility-first atomic preference
options.body: Keep paths-only arming supported, but update agent/tool guidance and timeout/error handling to prefer existing atomic upload-with-trigger or direct input targeting with focused tests and live proof.

options.title: Retire paths-only arming
options.body: Require a trigger ref, inputRef, or element for upload flows and provide migration guidance for callers that depended on delayed arming.

options.title: Document recovery only
options.body: Leave runtime behavior unchanged and document stale-ref recovery plus selector/batch mitigations, accepting that the underlying dynamic-page flake can still happen.

recommendation.title: Compatibility-first atomic preference
recommendation.body: Keep paths-only arming supported, but update agent/tool guidance and timeout/error handling to prefer existing atomic upload-with-trigger or direct input targeting with focused tests and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is Browser upload product/API direction, and central file history points most strongly to this owner for that surface.
